rationale:
Issue #1 ('Encoding a struct with all `nil` properties') reports that encoding an all-nil struct emits the malformed table `||`/`||`/`||`. The minimized production patch is a single hunk in Sources/MarkCodable/Encoder/MarkKeyedEncoding.swift adding a `String?` overload of `encodeIfPresent` that forwards to `encodeNil(forKey:)` instead of silently dropping the key, which is exactly what makes the nil String column header appear. The trigger patch changes the expectation in testCodingOptionalKeysDefaultTypes from `||`/`||`/`||` to `|name|`/`|----|`/`|    |` and re-enables the round-trip assertion that was commented out with an explicit link to issue #1, so issue, trigger, and fix describe the same pre-existing defect. The patch is production-only, one hunk, additions only, with no refactor, formatting, config, or doc-only change; the inline TODO comment is part of the added method. Both triggers are unchanged upstream tests from the fixing commit exercising only the pre-existing public MarkEncoder.encode / MarkDecoder.decode surface, so they do not depend on any API introduced by the fix; the added `encodeIfPresent` overload is an internal protocol-conformance method, not a new public API the tests call. Strict machine evidence passes all gates in both original and post-minimization runs (build.both_versions, trigger.buggy_differential with both selectors reproduced, trigger.fixed_clean, trigger.deterministic with 4/4 fingerprint groups, 3 repetitions, 38 matrix runs, fixed full suite green). active_same_project_root_causes is empty, so #1 is not a duplicate; #27 (example-app keyNotFound on 'price') is a distinct decoder codingPath defect addressed by other commits in PR #28 and is not the root cause of this hunk.

Issue #1 ('Encoding a struct with all `nil` properties') reports that encoding an all-nil struct emits the malformed table `||`/`||`/`||`. The minimized production patch is a single hunk in Sources/MarkCodable/Encoder/MarkKeyedEncoding.swift adding a `String?` overload of `encodeIfPresent` that forwards to `encodeNil(forKey:)` instead of letting the protocol default silently drop the key, which is precisely the omission that produced empty header rows. The commit message ('encode table headers for empty string cells / Fixed #1') and traceability path fix_commit_to_issue confirm the same defect. The trigger tests are the unchanged upstream test edits from the same fixing commit: testCodingOptionalKeysDefaultTypes changes the expected encoding from `||` to `|name|`/`|----|`/`|    |` and re-enables the round-trip assertion that was commented out with an explicit link to issue #1, and testSingleOptionalString has its `// FIXME: This currently fails` marker removed. Both exercise only pre-existing public API (MarkEncoder.encode, MarkDecoder.decode) and local fixtures; the patch introduces no new production API for the tests to call, since `encodeIfPresent` is an internal KeyedEncodingContainerProtocol requirement invoked through synthesized Codable conformance. The patch contains no refactor, formatting, feature, documentation, or configuration change; the only added comment is the inline TODO within the new method body. Both strict evidence sets (original and post-minimization) report passed=true with no failed checks: build on both revisions, buggy differential reproduction of both declared selectors, fixed clean on isolated/suite/reversed runs, determinism across 3 repetitions with 4 fingerprint groups, and a fixed full suite all green. The active same-project root cause registry is empty, so markcodable/markcodable#1 is not a duplicate.
